column1: # slug|impact,uniqueness,significance,experience,depth|category overrides or -|individual rationale
national-palace-museum|9.3,9.6,9.8,9.2,9.3|-|Unusually rich imperial art collection and cultural significance, but core visitor impact is not automatically above every great palace/museum worldwide.
taroko-national-park|9.5,9.5,9.1,9.3,9.4|-|Extraordinary marble gorge and high mountain system; avoid overlapping every Taroko Gorge component into park depth without distinction.
taroko-gorge|9.4,9.5,9.0,9.2,8.6|-|Spectacular specific marble gorge, with less independent exploration breadth than the entire Taroko National Park.

alishan-national-forest-recreation-area|9.2,9.3,8.6,9.0,9.1|-|Excellent giant-tree forests and cloudscapes, though one recreation area should not inherit the historic rail system or entire Alishan region.

alishan-forest-railway|8.7,9.0,8.9,8.7,8.2|history=9.2|Major scenic mountain-railway engineering and forest ride, but short railway experience should be benchmarked against Semmering Railway rather than Angkor-scale heritage.
yushan-main-peak|9.3,9.2,9.0,9.0,8.4|-|National high point offers major alpine challenge; peak viewpoint/trek is narrower than all Yushan National Park habitats.
yushan-national-park|9.2,9.3,9.0,9.0,9.2|-|Major high-elevation habitats and trekking range, without transferring each mountain summit's unique merit to every dimension.
shei-pa-national-park|9.1,9.2,8.7,8.8,9.0|-|Outstanding mountain and forest reserve, with slightly less global historical/scientific singularity than the top reference parks.
fo-guang-shan-buddha-museum|8.9,8.9,8.6,9.0,8.9|-|Monumental modern Buddhist complex and engaging museum, but its age and global heritage status differ from Angkor or ancient temples.
taipei-101|9.0,8.8,8.1,9.0,8.0|-|Iconic modern engineering and city view, but a single skyscraper visit has limited depth and less global historical significance.
xueshan-main-peak|8.9,8.9,8.5,8.9,8.3|-|High mountain climb and scenery, with much less diverse discovery than all of Shei-Pa National Park.
hehuanshan-mountain-area|8.9,8.7,8.1,8.9,8.3|-|Accessible alpine panoramas and hiking, but neither uniqueness nor historical significance equals globally singular mountain parks.
beigang-chaotian-temple|8.7,8.9,9.0,8.7,8.2|-|Major Taiwanese pilgrimage temple but less singular globally than much larger surviving sacred ensembles.
penghu-islands|8.8,9.0,8.4,8.9,8.8|-|Significant island group and basalt coast, while individual island sites should not inherit whole-archipelago exploration depth.
green-island|8.7,8.9,8.2,8.8,8.4|-|Valuable marine habitat and modern historical sites, without treating island size as worldwide uniqueness.
yehliu-geopark|8.9,9.1,8.5,8.9,8.1|-|Striking sea-eroded rock formations with memorable visit, but contained geopark depth below vast natural landscapes.

orchid-island-lanyu|9.0,9.4,8.9,8.9,8.6|-|Retain distinctive inhabited volcanic island, Tao maritime traditions and endemic biodiversity; unlike a beach stop this is a whole culturally meaningful island and nature destination. Source: https://twh.boch.gov.tw/taiwan/intro.aspx?id=11&lang=en_us

tainan-confucius-temple|8.7,8.9,9.1,8.8,8.0|history=9.1|Taiwan's first Confucian temple anchors local education and cultural history; global history category 9.5 was too high against Confucius hometown temple in Qufu or ancient capital ensembles. Source: https://taiwangods.moi.gov.tw/html/landscape_EN/1_0011.aspx?i=74

qingshui-cliffs|9.0,9.0,8.1,8.8,7.5|nature=9.2,photography=9.3|Dramatic Pacific-facing coastal cliffs within Taroko National Park, but short stopping-point panoramas and visitor breadth are below entire Taroko Gorge and large protected coastlines. Source: https://www.taroko.gov.tw/en/trailsAttractions/scenic-spots/80

national-taichung-theater|8.8,9.1,8.4,9.1,8.4|-|Retain excellent contemporary building designed by Toyo Ito; architecturally distinctive curvilinear theater interior genuinely merits high architecture category despite moderate broad world history significance. Source: https://www.npac-ntt.org/en/about/architecture/design

national-museum-of-taiwan-history|8.6,8.7,8.9,8.7,8.8|history=9.1|Important national history collection with substantial educational depth, but a strong local museum does not automatically merit 9.5 world-comparative history category alongside the great imperial art collections. Source: https://www.nmth.gov.tw/en/

zhaishan-tunnel|8.3,8.8,8.7,8.3,7.0|history=8.9|Noteworthy Kinmen military maritime supply tunnel built amid cross-strait tensions after 1958; limited contained visit and regional military context do not justify 9.5 world-historic category. Source: https://www.kmnp.gov.tw/en/titlelist/faq/2882

anping-old-fort|8.4,8.4,8.9,8.4,7.4|history=9.0|Fort Zeelandia was historically significant to Dutch Taiwan, but only limited original fort fabric survives and substantial modern repair/reconstruction reduces uniqueness and physical exploration. Source: https://twtainan.net/en/attractions/detail/4493/

weiwuying-national-kaohsiung-center-for-the-arts|8.6,8.9,8.4,9.0,8.8|-|Retain unusual contemporary performance complex with four venues under banyan-inspired roof; do not count every live performance as permanent sightseeing depth, but acknowledge large architecture. Source: https://www.npac-weiwuying.org/about?lang=en

taipei-zoo|8.2,7.8,8.0,8.7,9.0|-|Retain category-family and depth for a complete zoological institution with numerous animal habitats; earlier short-visit flag was a false positive because this record covers entire zoo, not one exhibit. Source: https://english.zoo.gov.taipei/cp.aspx?n=4AC205302039EC51&s=56D8655A57FA9A82

sun-moon-lake|8.8,8.7,8.2,9.0,8.8|nature=9.1,photography=9.1|Sun Moon Lake is an excellent and well-developed alpine lake tourism region with boats, cycling routes and surrounding temples, but worldwide scenic lake comparisons do not justify overall uniqueness 9.0 or every core field 9+. Source: https://www.sunmoonlake.gov.tw/en/

kinmen-national-park|8.6,8.6,8.9,8.6,8.5|history=9.3,nature=8.7|Kinmen National Park preserves distinctive Cold War-era forts, traditional settlements and coastal landscapes, but regional military significance and visitor breadth should not be treated as unique on a global 9.0 scale. Source: https://www.kmnp.gov.tw/en/

chiang-kai-shek-memorial-hall|8.7,8.5,9.0,8.7,8.2|history=9.1,architecture=9.1|Taipei's prominent national Chiang Kai-shek memorial and Liberty Square have strong political and architectural context, although a single memorial hall is less universally singular and deep than a large museum or multi-site heritage ensemble. Source: https://www.cksmh.gov.tw/en/

kenting-national-park|9.2,9.2,8.8,9.3,9.3|-|Kenting encompasses southern Taiwan's tropical shoreline, uplifted reef ecosystems, forests and multi-spot water recreation, with substantially greater depth than a single Kenting beach; region has strong but not globally unique biodiversity. Source: https://www.dbnsa.gov.tw/en/attraction/AttractionAreaPage?a=146

yangmingshan-national-park|9.1,9.1,9.0,9.2,9.0|-|Yangmingshan uniquely combines accessible active fumaroles, volcanic terrain, hot springs and trails near Taipei; natural scientific breadth merits strong scores while it remains smaller than vast global volcano parks. Source: https://www.ymsnp.gov.tw/en/sglarticle/volcanic-activities

matsu-islands|8.8,9.1,8.8,9.0,9.2|-|Matsu's several islands combine historic stone villages, military tunnels, coastal nature and bioluminescent seas, providing wider multi-day discovery than a single coastal fort or beach. Source: https://www.matsu-nsa.gov.tw/en-US/service/guidepack

east-rift-valley-national-scenic-area|8.8,8.9,8.2,9.1,9.4|-|Taiwan East Rift Valley is a long Hualien-Taitung scenic driving and cycling corridor with agriculture, mountains and villages; depth arises from multi-day exploration, not from one historically unique landmark. Source: https://www.erv-nsa.gov.tw/en/

chimei-museum|8.9,9.0,8.6,9.3,9.1|-|Tainan's Chimei Museum has an unusually broad Taiwanese private collection of Western art, instruments, arms, fossils and taxidermy, yielding stronger museum depth than a local specialty display, but not a world-dominant national heritage collection. Source: https://www.chimeimuseum.com.tw/en

jiaming-lake|9.0,9.0,8.4,8.8,8.5|-|Jiaming is a remote alpine lake approached on a demanding multi-day mountain trail, with strong scenery and trekking but far smaller global ecological significance than an entire high-mountain national park. Source: https://recreation.forest.gov.tw/en/Trail/RT?tr_id=139

921-earthquake-museum|8.7,9.2,9.4,9.1,8.5|-|The 921 Earthquake Museum preserves the actual 1999 Chi-Chi earthquake fault rupture and damaged school, giving unusually strong educational and scientific significance relative to small conventional memorial exhibits. Source: https://www.nmns.edu.tw/en/visit/explore-our-parks/park_921/index.html

alishan-giant-trees-trail|8.8,9.0,8.5,9.2,7.9|-|Alishan Giant Trees Trail passes many old-growth red cypress specimens and shrine landscape, a distinctive forest walk that should not inherit the much larger forest recreation area or Alishan railway's independent depth. Source: https://www.forest.gov.tw/en/0002777

chihkan-tower|8.6,8.9,9.2,9.1,7.9|-|Chihkan is the surviving and extensively modified site of 17th-century Dutch Fort Provintia in Tainan, historically important for colonial encounters but a compact single memorial building rather than a vast fortress complex. Source: https://historic.tainan.gov.tw/index.php?id=189&index=5&lang=en&option=module&task=pageinfo

xiaoliuqiu-island|8.7,8.8,8.1,9.1,8.6|-|Xiaoliuqiu features warm coastal reefs, regular green-sea-turtle encounters and compact island routes; its marine visitor experience is strong but not as globally singular as very large ocean biodiversity reserves. Source: https://www.dbnsa.gov.tw/en/PlanTrip/Articles?a=428

qinbi-village|8.7,9.1,8.8,9.0,8.1|-|Qinbi's hillside traditional stone houses overlooking the sea are a preserved Matsu heritage settlement, distinctively photogenic but narrower and less internationally historic than larger complete old towns. Source: https://www.matsu-nsa.gov.tw/en-US/service/guidepack

swallow-grotto-taroko|9.0,9.2,8.5,8.9,7.4|-|Swallow Grotto is a spectacular focused Taroko marble-gorge viewpoint and cliff trail, not the entire gorge or national park; official Taroko Park reports continued earthquake-related closure, which must be conveyed separately from intrinsic ratings. Source: https://www.taroko.gov.tw/en/trailsAttractions/scenic-spots/134

lukang-longshan-temple|8.8,9.1,9.2,8.8,8.1|-|Lukang's Longshan Temple preserves refined traditional Taiwanese Buddhist timber architecture and historic craftsmanship, with strong cultural significance but less ground coverage than great temple complexes. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lukang_Longshan_Temple

smangus-ancient-cypress-forest|8.9,9.3,8.6,8.7,8.8|-|Smangus contains giant old-growth red-cypress forest reached through remote Atayal mountain territory, a substantial forest walk rather than a casual scenic garden, with strong ecology but not country-scale park depth.

dajia-jenn-lann-temple|8.7,9.0,9.3,9.0,8.3|-|Dajia Jenn Lann Temple is a major Taiwanese Mazu pilgrimage center with an exceptionally large annual procession, giving wider living religious influence than a small ornamental urban shrine. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dajia_Jenn_Lann_Temple

lukang-tianhou-temple|8.7,8.8,9.0,8.8,8.0|-|Lukang Tianhou Temple is an important historic Mazu sanctuary with ornamented Taiwanese temple craftsmanship, while one courtyard offers less discovery than an entire historic port district. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lukang_Tianhou_Temple

national-museum-of-marine-biology-and-aquarium|8.6,8.5,8.8,9.2,9.3|-|Taiwan's major marine-biology museum and aquarium contains large themed tanks and research-oriented exhibits, yielding deep family/science visitation but internationally comparable aquariums. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Marine_Biology_and_Aquarium

qimei-island|8.3,8.5,7.8,8.8,8.4|-|Qimei is a small inhabited Penghu island known for historic fishing stone weirs, coastal rocks and quiet villages; rewarding island excursion without the ecological breadth of the whole archipelago. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qimei

penghu-basalt-columns|8.8,9.3,8.8,8.9,8.0|-|Penghu's columnar basalt sea cliffs and island formations show unusual volcanic cooling geometry, exceptional regional geology but a collection of short coastal viewpoints, not the whole archipelago visit.

turtle-island|8.7,9.0,8.6,8.7,8.2|-|Guishan Turtle Island is an offshore volcanic island with sulfur vents, marine wildlife and restricted boat access; geological distinctiveness is stronger than a generic recreational beach.

zhaori-hot-springs-green-island|8.5,9.5,8.0,8.8,7.5|-|Green Island's Zhaori hot spring is a very rare seawater thermal bathing site, memorable in its natural ocean-facing setting but a contained bathing excursion rather than extensive geological exploration.

green-island-human-rights-memorial-park|8.8,9.3,9.6,8.7,8.8|-|Green Island's former political prison memorial interprets Taiwan's White Terror and democratic transition in historical prison structures, carrying profound national history beyond a simple island viewpoint.

longshan-temple-taipei|8.8,9.2,9.2,9.1,8.4|-|Taipei's Longshan Temple is a prominent active eighteenth-century religious sanctuary with richly ornamented halls and local ritual life, culturally deep but not a gigantic ancient temple complex. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longshan_Temple_(Taipei)

lala-mountain-giant-trees|8.7,9.1,8.6,8.6,8.3|-|Lalashan forest trails pass numerous giant ancient red cypress trees, a strong individual old-growth forest attraction that should not inherit every surrounding protected mountain's full natural significance.

wufeng-lin-family-mansion|8.6,9.0,9.2,8.9,8.7|-|The Wufeng Lin Family Mansion and Garden preserves a large Qing-era Taiwanese family compound and architectural/social heritage, more extensive than an individual historic house. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wufeng_Lin_Family_Mansion_and_Garden

chung-tai-chan-monastery|8.5,9.2,8.3,8.8,8.7|-|Chung Tai Chan is a monumental contemporary Buddhist monastery with striking modern vertical architecture and religious activity, unusual as a new complex but less centuries-deep than ancient temples. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chung_Tai_Chan_Monastery

national-museum-of-natural-science|8.9,8.7,9.0,9.2,9.5|-|Taichung's National Museum of Natural Science encompasses scientific galleries, botany and large permanent exhibits, giving substantial educational visitor depth without imperial-art-level singularity. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Museum_of_Natural_Science

tunnel-of-nine-turns|8.8,9.0,8.4,8.6,7.0|-|Taroko's Tunnel of Nine Turns allows close views of dramatic polished marble cliffs, yet the individual tunnel trail has limited length and should not inherit the entire Taroko Gorge's exploration score; check earthquake-related access separately.

sanxiantai-island-and-bridge|8.7,8.7,7.8,8.9,7.7|-|Sanxiantai features an iconic eight-arched pedestrian bridge connecting an island with Pacific rock formations; photogenic coastal stroll with modest standalone cultural significance.

national-palace-museum-southern-branch|8.6,8.8,8.8,8.9,8.8|-|The southern National Palace Museum branch near Chiayi presents Asian cultural collections in a purpose-built museum, with meaningful gallery depth but less defining imperial collection breadth than Taipei's main museum. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southern_Branch_of_the_National_Palace_Museum

koxinga-shrine|8.4,8.7,9.2,8.7,8.0|-|Tainan's Koxinga Shrine commemorates the Ming loyalist who ended Dutch rule of Taiwan, important nationally while the single shrine precinct is modest compared with major multi-monument heritage areas. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koxinga_Shrine

lukang-old-street|8.6,8.7,8.4,8.8,8.0|-|Lukang Old Street retains narrow trading lanes, traditional shops and historic port-town atmosphere, meaningful as a district walk but not the entire preserved urban center or all of its temples.

gold-museum-jinguashi|8.5,9.0,8.6,8.8,8.9|-|The Gold Museum preserves a distinctive former mining settlement and mine-tunnel exhibits near Jinguashi, with valuable industrial history and a broader visit than a single mining artifact.

guningtou-battle-museum|8.4,8.7,9.1,8.5,7.8|-|Kinmen's Guningtou Battle Museum documents the 1949 battle with military displays and commemoration, nationally consequential but physically a focused military museum. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guningtou_Battle_Museum

pier-2-art-center|8.5,8.4,8.0,9.0,8.9|-|Kaohsiung's Pier-2 is a large repurposed warehouse arts district with sculptures, galleries and creative shops, a rewarding urban experience but with limited ancient historical significance. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pier-2_Art_Center

xitou-nature-education-area|8.5,8.4,8.4,9.0,8.7|-|Xitou offers forest walks, research-era tree plantings and well-developed visitor trails, giving worthwhile forest-education depth without matching the rare giant-tree ecology of primeval reserves. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xitou_Nature_Education_Area

jiufen-old-street|8.8,9.1,8.2,9.0,8.0|-|Jiufen Old Street has distinctive steep mining-era lanes, teahouses and hillside-coast views, highly atmospheric while not inheriting the entire wider Jiufen town's history and nature. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiufen_Old_Street

shanlinxi-forest-recreation-area|8.7,8.6,8.1,8.9,8.6|-|Shanlinxi Forest Recreation Area offers broad mountain forest walks, waterfalls and seasonal flowers, strong sustained scenic visitation but less worldwide botanical rarity than protected old-growth forests. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanlinxi_Forest_Recreation_Area

dalongdong-baoan-temple|8.6,9.1,9.2,8.9,8.0|-|Dalongdong Baoan Temple is a well-preserved Taipei religious complex recognized for skilled restoration and rich Taiwanese temple craftsmanship, but one temple alone has modest exploration breadth. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dalongdong_Baoan_Temple

maolin-purple-butterfly-valley|8.7,9.2,8.8,8.5,8.3|-|Maolin's winter congregation of purple crow butterflies is an unusual seasonal migration phenomenon, ecologically distinctive but wildlife viewing depends on conditions and does not cover a huge park.

xiaoyoukeng-volcanic-area|8.6,9.0,8.5,8.8,7.7|-|Xiaoyoukeng contains accessible sulfur fumaroles and geothermally active slopes in Yangmingshan, an unusual local geology stop but narrower than the entire national park.

shakadang-trail|8.8,9.0,8.0,8.7,8.0|-|Shakadang follows exceptionally turquoise Taroko creek and steep marble gorge walls, but its individual trail has less scope than the park and earthquake damage can restrict access. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakadang_Trail

shuitou-historic-village|8.5,8.8,8.5,8.7,8.1|-|Shuitou in Kinmen preserves a cluster of merchant and overseas-Chinese traditional houses, atmospheric as a compact village walk without entire Kinmen island's martial history.

longpan-park|8.6,8.7,7.6,8.8,7.5|-|Longpan Park has windswept grassland terraces facing the Pacific near Kenting, a memorable cliff-edge stop with limited world historical significance or long exploration depth. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Longpan_Park

zhushan-sunrise-viewing-platform|8.9,8.5,7.7,8.8,7.2|-|Zhushan's sunrise platforms provide dramatic Alishan cloud-sea morning views, though one viewing station should not inherit the entire forest recreation area or railway's historical importance.

formosan-aboriginal-culture-village|8.4,8.2,7.5,8.9,8.8|-|The Formosan Aboriginal Culture Village combines interpretive Indigenous-themed exhibits with amusement rides, broad family entertainment but separate from living Indigenous communities' genuine historic heritage.

baiyang-waterfall-trail|8.6,8.9,7.8,8.7,8.0|-|Baiyang Waterfall Trail passes tunnels and water curtains within Taroko's dramatic cliffs, a memorable hiking component but a smaller attraction than Taroko National Park and vulnerable to earthquake closure.

british-consulate-at-takow|8.3,8.6,8.8,8.7,7.7|-|The former British Consulate at Takow is an early Western-style hillside building overlooking Kaohsiung harbor, combining port-trade history with coastal views but relatively limited indoor museum space. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Former_British_Consulate_at_Takao

dihua-street|8.4,8.5,8.8,8.9,8.6|-|Taipei's Dihua Street retains traditional commercial shophouses, herbal traders and dried-goods shops, an extensive living street experience with stronger cultural depth than a single market stall.

aowanda-national-forest-recreation-area|8.5,8.8,8.2,8.8,8.7|-|Aowanda is known for mountain maple forests, suspension bridge views and seasonal river valley walks, a worthwhile forest recreation area but not a globally defining protected biome. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aowanda_National_Forest_Recreation_Area

gaomei-wetlands|8.8,8.8,8.6,9.0,8.0|-|Gaomei Wetlands is a tidal shore habitat with panoramic boardwalks, large wind turbines and migratory birds, giving exceptional sunset experience without the ecosystem breadth of the world's largest wetlands. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaomei_Wetlands

qixing-mountain-main-peak|8.6,8.6,8.3,8.9,7.8|-|Taipei's Qixing summit is a distinctive volcanic high point with accessible fumarole-area trails, but this one climb should not inherit Yangmingshan National Park's full geothermal landscape scope.

penghu-tianhou-temple|8.2,8.8,9.0,8.4,7.3|-|Magong Tianhou Temple is among Taiwan's oldest major Mazu temples and a historic Penghu maritime-pilgrimage site, but compact grounds have less visitor depth than a large temple ensemble. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penghu_Tianhou_Temple

anping-tree-house|8.5,9.0,8.0,8.7,7.7|-|Anping Tree House is an atmospheric old warehouse almost enclosed by banyan roots, highly distinctive visually but limited as an independent historic collection. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anping_Tree_House

eternal-spring-shrine|8.5,8.7,8.6,8.5,6.9|-|Taroko's Eternal Spring Shrine commemorates workers lost building the Cross-Island Highway and sits against a waterfall cliff; evocative single viewpoint, not the entire park and with earthquake access issues.

wuling-farm|8.4,8.5,7.9,8.9,8.7|-|Wuling Farm is an upland valley recreational landscape with cherry blossoms, hiking and agriculture, offering extended seasonal nature visits but modest global ecological singularity. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wuling_Farm

twin-hearts-stone-weir|8.2,8.8,8.2,8.4,6.5|-|Qimei's double-heart fishing weir is distinctive traditional coastal engineering and a photogenic heritage landmark, but the single stone structure offers a short visit relative to the whole Penghu island system.

beihai-tunnel-nangan|8.3,8.9,8.8,8.5,7.2|-|Nangan Beihai Tunnel is a remarkable coastal rock-cut military boat tunnel from the Cold War era, unusual engineering but a confined underground stop rather than the full Matsu island history.

guanziling-mud-hot-springs|8.5,9.2,7.9,8.8,7.4|-|Guanziling is famous for unusual naturally muddy hot springs and bath houses, a distinctive geothermal wellness attraction but not a broad geology field area or historically singular spa town.

hsinchu-city-god-temple|8.2,8.5,8.9,8.6,7.7|-|Hsinchu's City God Temple has a prominent Taoist ritual role and dense traditional food-market setting, meaningfully cultural but smaller in regional reach than Dajia's immense Mazu pilgrimage.

shuinandong-thirteen-level-remains|8.5,9.0,8.8,8.6,7.0|-|The Thirteen-Level mining smelter ruins above the northeast coast are a dramatic abandoned industrial silhouette, but most appreciation comes from exterior views rather than deep museum visitation.

siouguluan-river-rafting|8.7,8.6,7.8,9.2,8.3|-|Xiuguluan River offers one of Taiwan's better-established white-water rafting trips through scenic eastern coastal mountains, with experiential strength but ordinary world river-history significance.

sun-moon-lake-wenwu-temple|8.4,8.5,8.4,8.8,7.7|-|Wenwu Temple combines elaborate Chinese-style religious architecture with sweeping Sun Moon Lake terraces, striking as a standalone temple view but not the entire lake's varied visitor experience. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sun_Moon_Lake_Wen_Wu_Temple

juguang-tower|8.0,8.3,8.5,8.3,7.0|-|Kinmen's Juguang Tower is an iconic modern war-era monument with island history displays and an observation level, regionally important but a relatively compact tower. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juguang_Tower

juming-museum|8.5,9.0,8.5,8.8,8.8|-|Ju Ming Museum has a substantial sculpture park and artist-designed outdoor setting, giving a more spatially immersive contemporary-art experience than a small indoor gallery. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ju_Ming_Museum

lintianshan-forestry-culture-garden|8.1,8.7,8.6,8.5,8.0|-|Lintianshan preserves an old logging-village and forestry infrastructure setting in eastern Taiwan, valuable industrial-social history but smaller than a full national forestry museum.

dragon-and-tiger-pagodas|8.5,8.5,7.9,8.8,6.8|-|Kaohsiung's colorful Dragon and Tiger Pagodas are photogenic towers on Lotus Pond with symbolic entrances, fun for a short visit but not centuries-old world-defining religious heritage.

raohe-street-night-market|8.4,8.4,8.0,9.1,8.0|-|Raohe is a focused, lively traditional Taipei night market offering numerous food stalls and evening atmosphere, excellent culinary experience but limited historical or archaeological distinctiveness. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raohe_Street_Night_Market

fort-san-domingo|8.2,8.6,8.8,8.5,8.0|-|Fort San Domingo in Tamsui represents layered Spanish, Dutch, British and Taiwanese colonial administration, with historic buildings and coastal panorama but limited grounds compared with citywide fortification systems.

taipei-confucius-temple|8.2,8.4,8.6,8.7,7.9|-|Taipei Confucius Temple provides a traditionally designed tranquil scholarly shrine with seasonal ceremonies, valuable cultural interpretation but below the global original Qufu Confucius Temple's significance. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taipei_Confucius_Temple

wulai-waterfall|8.6,8.4,7.5,8.9,7.5|-|Wulai Waterfall is a tall and scenic cascade reached from a mountain hot-spring village, with a convenient viewpoint and trolley context but limited standalone ecological rarity. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wulai_Waterfall
